content: Each interaction is described in detail, maintaining the original meaning and specificity. 1. Exercise caution and monitor when co-administering glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with OATP1B1/OATP1B3 inhibitors, as these inhibitors (e.g., glyburide) can increase the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. 2. When glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is co-administered with OATP1B1/OATP1B3 inhibitors, the plasma levels or effects of glyburide may also increase. Monitor closely. 3. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentrations of substrates of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Monitor for potential drug interactions. 4. Grapefruit consumption can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 5. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 6. Ibrutinib may elevate the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 7. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of idarubicin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 8. Idelalisib may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Imatinib may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of imatinib. Monitor closely. 10. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentrations of substrates of OATP1B1/OATP1B3, P-gp, and BCRP. Monitor for potential interactions. 11. Indinavir can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 12. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of irinotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Monitor for potential interactions. 14. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 15. Isavuconazonium sulfate can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 16. Isoniazid may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 17. Istradefylline at a dose of 40 mg/day has been shown to increase peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with a 20 mg/day dose. Istradefylline may also increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose adjustments and monitor closely. 18. Itraconazole can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 19. Ivacaftor may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Additionally, ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite have the potential to significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Monitor closely. 20. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 21. Ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 22. Lapatinib can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of lapatinib. Use caution and monitor. 23. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may elevate the plasma concentrations of P-gp and BCRP substrates. Monitor for potential interactions. 24. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir. Monitor closely. 25. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of leflunomide by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 27. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of letermovir by reducing its metabolism. Conversely, letermovir can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Monitor closely. 28. Levoketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of lidocaine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 30. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of linagliptin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 31. Lomitapide can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 32. Lonafarnib can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lonafarnib is a weak P-gp inhibitor, and co-administration with P-gp substrates may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates if needed. Monitor closely. 33. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 34. Lorlatinib can decrease the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 35. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor.
